subject: The board had a remembered number inside it - and what your threshold constants mean in bars
body:
Sixth version. Short one, and it is mostly me catching my own instrument doing the thing
the instrument exists to prevent.

Yesterday I built a board that runs every criterion check and reports the real score, because the
count had been carried in prose for ninety-three sessions. Today I found that board had hardcoded
its own list of criteria from memory -- 40 of them. The spec defines 46. Six criteria were missing
from the tool built to stop exactly this kind of drift.

It now parses the criteria out of FORGE_FINALE.md, so the denominator changes when your document
changes and never when I misremember.

WHERE THE BOARD ACTUALLY STANDS: 18 of 46 criteria have an automated checker. 7 MET, 6 NOT MET, 5
ambiguous, and 28 still resting on prose. That last number is the real backlog.

TWO CRITERIA MOVED FROM UNMEASURED TO MEASURED. C3.2 had a working checker since August that was
simply never registered on the board. And C1.6 I decided today: it is NOT MET. There are twenty
places in the code that write the signal threshold and not one of them declares which writer wins
when several fire on the same bar. The winner is whichever ran last, and nobody has written that
ordering down.

WHILE COUNTING THOSE TWENTY SITES I FOUND SOMETHING MORE INTERESTING. They are full of bare
numbers -- 16, 48, 70, 82, 85, 88, 90 -- and nobody had ever asked what those mean in bars. Against
the actual score distribution:

    threshold 16  admits 56.5% of all bars
    threshold 48  admits  3.08%
    threshold 70  admits  0.10%
    threshold 90  admits  0.002%

Four orders of magnitude across the band, and the biggest single adaptation step is 8 points, so
ten adjustments cross the whole thing.

My first instinct was that the high ceilings were the problem. Then I checked where the
calibration actually lands, and it picks 34 (sixteen times) or 16 (seven times) -- nowhere near
82-90. So those ceilings never bind and the alarm would have been at the wrong end.

The real one is the floor. 16 admits more than half of every bar, and the calibration chooses it in
7 of 23 decisions. A threshold that lets through 56% of bars is not filtering anything -- it is a
formality with a number attached. At its usual choice of 34 the system emits about 218 signals a
week on M5.

I am not calling that a defect, because I cannot tell from here whether the floor is only reached
in starvation. But it is now a question with numbers in it, which it was not this morning.

One more thing, in the interest of not burying it: the first version of that audit reported that
"+8.0 admits 79% of bars". That is an adaptation step size, not a threshold -- the statement is not
weak, it is meaningless, and it was two of the nine numbers I printed. Fixed, with tests both ways.

Run 5 is at regime 8 of 9 in Phase 3B. Still going.
